Subject: Demo request — GitHub integration (OSS)

Hey Mateo —

Quick note: I signed up via the self-serve flows and poked around the GitHub integration docs. OpenForge is evaluating a repo-level code-intel + CI-cost reduction workflow and we want to see Redwood's GitHub Actions integration in action. Main asks:
- Does Redwood support in-repo config + Actions-side deployment?
- Can we run private scanning (on our runners) or is it only hosted?
- How do you handle token scopes and least-privilege for org-level installs?

We'd love a 30–45m demo with an FE engineer and our infra lead. Available windows next week: Wed/Thu mornings PST.

Thanks — happy to fold in our SW eng.

— Emilia
Emilia Torres
Head of Platform, OpenForge
emilia@openforge.dev

Hi Emilia —

Thanks for signing up and for the clear context. Happy to set up a demo focused on Actions + repo-level config. Quick answers up front: we support both org apps and PAT-based installs; private scanning on customer runners is possible via our agent (we can walk through tradeoffs). Token-scope best practices vary by installs — Laura (cc'd) can cover secure installation patterns.

Availability: I can do Wednesday 2027-04-07 09:30–10:15 PT or Thursday 2027-04-08 10:00–10:45 PT. Do either of those work for your eng + infra leads? If not, drop a couple of times and I’ll circulate a calendar invite.

Also, is there any non-disclosure area we should avoid on the call (sensitive IP, or contract/legal folks who should be included)?

Best,
Mateo
SDR, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Demo request — GitHub integration (OSS)

Hi Emilia / team —

Great — looking forward to the session. I attached a simple architecture sketch and a one-pager that covers install modes and token guidance (see attachments). Short takeaways:
- We support a lightweight agent for self-hosted runners (no data plane traffic leaves your VPC unless you opt-in).
- Org App installs work for org-level policies; granular repo installs work too if you prefer least-privilege.
- For our demo we'll show a repo-to-Actions flow and a quick look at SLOs and cost controls.

Proposed agenda (30–45m):
1) Quick intros (5m)
2) Demo: install + run on self-hosted runner (15–20m)
3) Q&A: token scopes, data flow, multi-repo policies (10m)
4) Next steps: trial plan & PoC checklist (5m)

Attachment: integration-arch.png (diagram)
Attachment: redwood-github-quickstart.pdf (one-pager)

One small ask — Mei is in CET; can we confirm the timezone as PT? The calendar invite should include automatic timezone conversion.

Thanks,
Laura
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
